title: Console accent harmonization and progressive elevation for multi-brand dark themes
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Unify how accent colors from multiple customer brand palettes are mapped into the console dark themes while preserving accessible contrast and predictable component elevation behavior. Deliver token mapping rules, component override patterns (buttons, tables, charts), and a small component shim library for progressive darkening/elevation to avoid brand accents drifting into illegible hues on low-surface contrast backgrounds.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical token mapping doc exists that shows how any 3rd-party brand primary/accent colors map to: surface-accent, accent-foreground, accent-muted, and accent-outline across light and dark themes.

Button, table row, and chart series examples render correctly in dark theme for 10 sample brand accents with automated contrast checks >= 4.5:1 for body text and >= 3:1 for UI controls where WCAG allows.
A minimal CSS/JS shim (component-level overrides) is implemented and released behind a feature flag that progressively darkens accents based on elevation and background luminance.
Design tokens are added to the token library and documented in Figma with usage guidelines and migration notes for existing components.
Performance regression: console render performance for pages with multiple accent variants shows <5% change compared to baseline.
PM/Eng signoff recorded and one cross-functional demo held with QA and Accessibility team.
design_notes: Problem: brand accents often sit at fixed HSL values. On dark surfaces they can appear overly saturated or lose contrast with text. Our previous approach created inconsistent overlays per component and required too many brand-specific tokens.

Approach: introduce a small neutral scaffold for accents in dark themes. Each brand primary maps to a set of derived accent tokens computed by: (1) normalize to perceptual lightness (L*), (2) generate scaffold anchors (accent-surface, accent-foreground, accent-muted) using fixed delta offsets, (3) apply progressive darkening based on elevation bands using alpha overlays and slight desaturation.

Elevation model: use three elevation bands for small UI surfaces (0/1/2). Higher elevation increases contrast with accent-surface by applying overlay +8% lightness per band and +6% desaturation to avoid neon effects.

Chart guidance: avoid using raw brand primary for thin stroke series. Use accent-muted for strokes and reserve accent-foreground for filled series or strong highlights. Provide fallback palette generation for up to 6 series from a single accent using hue-preserving lightness steps.
Table rows: preserve zebra/hover patterns by applying subtle overlay multipliers on accent-muted; ensure selected-row states maintain text contrast >= 4.5:1.
Buttons: primary filled buttons use accent-foreground on accent-surface. Outline/ghost variants use accent-outline derived from accent-muted with 60% alpha against underlying surface.

Trade-offs considered: full brand tokenization (heavy, many tokens) vs. derived scaffold (lighter, consistent). We chose derived scaffold to minimize token explosion and runtime overhead while offering deterministic results for any incoming brand color.

Accessibility: integrated automated color contrast checks into CI for sample accents. For extreme accents that fail thresholds, we will surface a warning and recommend adjusted tokens to the customer via Console branding UX.
Migration: add token aliases so existing components can switch to new tokens gradually. Provide a codemod script for button classes.
